texts.2d69495e9021:
Access to the data will enable the Local Authority to undertake locally-focused and locally-responsive analyses of health status and health outcomes. For example, the data will be used to produce analyses of health inequalities for non-standard geographies and for specific social or ethnic groups in the local population to help ensure that the health challenges facing the local population – particularly the most disadvantaged – have been identified and responded to appropriately by the Local Authority and its partners.

It is recognised that in fulfilling its public health duties using HES data, the Local Authority will deliver significant benefits.  The Local Authority therefore commits in any renewal request to providing additional detail on benefits that relate to their local use of the data.

It has also been used in relation to shingles, flu and exploration of infant hospital attendance. All the analytical outputs have led to a greater understanding and depth of knowledge than possible without the data set which will lead to enhanced strategies and commissioning decisions.
texts.9d12cf19163e:
Feb 2021
Due to the pandemic a great deal of focus in 2020 was spent on other datasets. Please see the 2019/20 report on a more typical year of business for a more representative use of the datasets.

At Wiltshire Council in 2019/20 analysis was performed using the HES data sets to understand alcohol related admissions, falls admissions, intentional and accidental admissions at a local operational geographic level (as an aggregated figure to avoid disclosure with small number suppression) and at a CCG, group and locality level. It has also been used in relation to shingles, flu and exploration of infant hospital attendance. All the analytical outputs have led to a greater understanding and depth of knowledge than possible without the data set which will lead to enhanced strategies and commissioning decisions.
texts.aed593c28426:
Access to the data will enable the Local Authority to undertake locally-focused and locally-responsive analyses of health status and health outcomes. For example, the data will be used to produce analyses of health inequalities for non-standard geographies and for specific social or ethnic groups in the local population to help ensure that the health challenges facing the local population – particularly the most disadvantaged – have been identified and responded to appropriately by the Local Authority and its partners.

It is recognised that in fulfilling its public health duties using HES data, the Local Authority will deliver significant benefits.  The Local Authority therefore commits in any renewal request to providing additional detail on benefits that relate to their local use of the data.

At Wiltshire Council in 2016/17 analysis was performed using the HES data set to understand alcohol related admissions, falls admissions and intentional and accidental admissions at a local operational geographic level (as an aggregated figure to avoid disclosure with small number suppression). Some of this data supported a prioritisation process that has led community groups to be formed to combat local issues.
texts.c170c3ccdb87:
At Wiltshire Council in 2018/19 analysis was performed using the HES datasets to understand alcohol related admissions, falls admissions, intentional and accidental admissions at a local operational geographic level (as an aggregated figure to avoid disclosure with small number suppression) and at a CCG, group and locality level. It has also been used in air pollution research, cost-consequence analysis regarding falls and activity in records to outpatient and A&E attendances. All the analytical outputs have lead to a greater understanding and depth of knowledge than possible without the dataset which will lead to enhanced strategies and commissioning decisions.

During 2017/18 the HES extract data has been used for a number of projects. Firstly the extracts were used to explore hospital admissions for intentional and unintentional injuries in the 15-24 year olds. This report helped dispel some erroneous beliefs as to the reasons for these admissions and highlighted that a large proportion of the admissions were from intentional injuries. The HES extracts were used in the 2017 JSNA found on http://wiltshireintelligence.org.uk/key-issues/health-and-wellbeing/overview/ which outlined the health needs for Wiltshire. It was also used in some targeted work on falls in the elderly. Road accidents were also explored. There have been additional small requests for figures on specific diseases used for promotional work by the PH specialists and consultants.
